source.cells: A Brand AE-BM-H List 8430/8530 - Roughing - Contouring (printed p.1467); row '2 mm'; column 'Up to 45 HRC': Speed RPM 20850; Feed in/min 131.0; Cutting Speed header 425 - 500 SFM; Depth of Cut aa=0.15D, ar=0.2D

material.vendor_label: Tool Steels, Hardened Steels, Alloy Steels

vendor_notes: The above parameters are applicable to an overhang of 4xD maximum. When the overhang is longer, please reduce feed, speed, and cutting depth.
Use a rigid and precise machine and holder.
We suggest using air blow or MQL (mist).

The above parameters are standard starting values for contouring and side milling operations. If vibration or chatter occurs due to machine or part setup, please adjust the speed, feed, and depth of cut accordingly.
If contouring includes corners of radius less than 1.5 times the tool diameter, reduce speed and feed to 50-80% of above and reduce Ar to 20-60% of above.
When the part incline angle (beta) is more than 15 deg, reduce the speed to 40-60% of above parameters, the feed to 30-50% of above parameters, and Aa to 30-60% of above parameters.
If the cutting depth is small it is possible to increase the speed and feed above the recommended parameters.
rows.notes: Computed: SFM = 20850 rpm x pi x D / 12 = 429.8 (D = 0.07874 in); fz = 131.0 in/min / (20850 rpm x 4 flutes) = 0.00157 in/tooth. ap = aa -> 0.01181 in; ae = ar -> 0.01575 in. Metric part 8549602 (List 8530): D = 2.0 mm, lengths converted at 25.4 mm/in. Roughing/finishing 3D contouring of hardened steels with a 4-flute ball end mill; aa = axial depth, ar = radial depth as printed (aa/ar are given as multiples of the cutter diameter D). The sheet gives no separate effective-diameter rule; note 6 of the sheet reduces speed, feed and Aa for part incline angles above 15 deg. Depth-of-Cut cells of the Roughing page are merged across hardness columns; the assignment (D<6 / 6<=D tables to Up to 45 and 45-55 HRC, and to 55-62 HRC; aa=0.05D, ar=0.15D to 62-66 and 66-70 HRC) was read from the rendered page, so this row is flagged image for a second check. Neck diameter d1 and neck length L1 are the catalog values printed on the list (relieved neck); LB is set to L1.
